articleTitle: Physics-Based Compact Model for GaN-Based Non-linear Transmission Line Resistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel, comprehensive physics-based model for capturing non-ideal effects in GaN transmission line resistors for use in monolithic GaN integrated circuits. The model captures the important effects of non-linear resistance, including current saturation, self-heating and thermal coupling, and charge trapping, and is closely related to the industry-standard MVSG GaN HEMT Compact Model. Good agreement with measurement is achieved, validating the model and demonstrating scalability with bias, device dimensions and temperature. The results are applied to a simple power amplifier circuit to demonstrate the necessity of adopting an accurate non-linear resistor model in practical circuit design.

articleTitle: 140-GHz Transmit and Receive Front-end Circuits with 10.8-dBm Psat and 5.9-dB NF in a 45-nm BiCMOS SOI Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present the design and implementation of 140GHz Transmit/Receive (T/R) front-end circuits for D-band $(110-170 \mathrm{GHz}$) wireless communication or radar. Leveraging a state-of-the-art 45-nm BiCMOS SOI process, the FEM integrates a Low-Noise Amplifier (LNA), Power Amplifier (PA), and T/R switch. The LNA, featuring a hybrid cascode architecture, achieves a minimum noise figure (NF) of 4.5 dB at 144 GHz. The T/R switch featuring base matching exhibits an insertion loss of 1.4 dB and isolation exceeding 17 dB at 140 GHz. In receive (RX) mode, the measured gain is 7.7 dB and NF is 5.9 dB at 140 GHz. In transmit (TX) mode, the peak power-added efficiency (PAE) is 9.3% at a $4.5-\mathrm{dB}$ gain at 132 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Performance SiGe Heterojunction Phototransistor in a Commercial SiGe BiCMOS Platform for Free-Space Optical Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A high-performance SiGe heterojunction phototransistor (HPT) with peak responsivity of $12.5 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{W}$ at 850 nm and an optical transition frequency of 150 GHz is developed in a commercial SiGe BiCMOS technology platform by optimizing the lateral geometry of SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs). An optical receiver based on the proposed SiGe HPT with $\gt40 \mathrm{~dB} \Omega$ gain and 10 GHz bandwidth is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A 10 Gb/s, 120 GHz Compact and Energy-Efficient Harmonic-OOK Modulator using 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a compact and energy-efficient frequency multiplier with an embedded direct-digital harmonic on-off keying modulator. The multiplier uses a standing-wave resonator (SWR), features a half-wavelength varactor-loaded transmission line for efficient harmonic generation. Additionally, a novel OOK modulation technique has also been introduced, which modulates by switching a non-uniform impedance coupled line (NUiCL) filter, integrated with the frequency multiplier. The proposed modulator exhibits data rate of $10 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ with bit-errorrate (BER) of less than $10^{-9}$. The proposed harmonic modulator, fabricated using 90 nm Silicon-Germanium (SiGe) BiCMOS technology process, is purely passive. Nevertheless, it features a single stage buffer amplifier which consumes only 4 mW of DC power ($\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{DC}}$), resulting in an 8 dB conversion loss. The proposed circuit occupies a compact active area of $185 \mu \mathrm{~m} \times 350 \mu \mathrm{~m} \mathbf{(0. 0 6 5}$ $\mathbf{m m}^{2}$).

articleTitle: D-Band meets FinFET: Fully-Integrated Transmitter and Receiver Architectures for 100+Gb/s Links
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper highlights recent D-Band (110-170 GHz) transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) architectures which achieve 100+ Gb/s data rates. Such high data rates are achieved with efficiencies < 2 pJ/b while also integrating key building blocks required for end-to-end system - DAC, ADC, PLL. The TX employs a direct-conversion RF-DAC architecture and generates a 140 GHz LO signal from a 5.83 GHz input reference. It achieves peak data rates of 80/160 Gb/s (QPSK/16QAM) with an EVM of 17.9 dB and 1pJb efficiency at 160 Gb}/s. The RX integrates a direct-conversion architecture with wideband baseband, an LO gen identical to the TX, and a high-speed ADC. It achieves a peak data rate of 128 Gb/ with -15.2 dB EVM and 1.95pJ/b efficiency.

articleTitle: A 132-204 GHz Carrier Storage Frequency Divider with sub-50 Micro-Watt DC Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency divider by utilizing the carrier storage property in silicon PIN diodes. PIN diodes undergo reverse recovery under a large-signal RF drive. The proposed design utilizes this property and drives the diode into reverse recovery once in two cycles of RF input in order to generate a divide-by-two output. The circuit consumes near zero DC power since the diode is reverse-biased during division operation. Implemented in GlobalFoundries 90nm SiGe BiCMOS process, the proposed divider has a division range spanning 132 GHz to 204 GHz for an input signal of <-1 dBm and consumes 42 μW DC power. Experimental results show minor phase noise degradation upon division. This is the first demonstration of a carrier storage PIN diode divider in silicon. This work performs frequency division at the highest input frequency among all reported silicon-based dividers.

articleTitle: A 19.1-dBm-Linear 2-20 GHz N-path Down-converter in HRL 40-nm GaN for Resilient Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the potential for GaN Npath down-conversion mixers to operate linearly in the presence of 19.1 dBm in-band interference and >25 dBm out-of-band. We measured 4-10 dB NF across 2-20 GHz for this LNA-less 4-phase active-mixer receiver front-end including degradations due to non-negligible amplitude/phase imbalance introduced by the off-chip hybrid and balun modules used to generate quadrature gate drive from a 16 dBm single-ended source. The mixer consumes 25 mW with a 2.5 V drain bias to ensure low-loss hard-switching under sinusoidal drive (as opposed to non-overlapping digital pulses or resonant pseudo-pulses used in prior art N-path downconverters) delivering a 10 dB improvement in SFDR over 9.3x greater fractional bandwidth compared to previously reported GaN N-path down-converters. With 200 MHz instantaneous BW, the receiver front-end achieves a maximum 98 dB dynamic range under 3.5 dB NF desensitization caused by 15 dBm in-band interference. To quantify the utility of receivers for operating in the presence of high-power, co-site emitters we define a new FoM for emitter resilience that considers receiver sensitivity, power handling, and frequency coverage.

articleTitle: TCAD-Based Design of SiGe HBT Germanium Profiles via Bayesian Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work investigates the automatic design of silicon-germanium (SiGe) heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) germanium profiles utilizing Bayesian optimization in a commercial TCAD engine. The time-intensive nature of device simulation renders standard numerical optimization strategies infeasible, as gradients are expensive to approximate, and candidate objective functions, such as device minimum noise figure ($N F_{\text {min }}$), maximum transit frequency $\left(f_{T}\right)$, or breakdown voltage ($B V_{C E O}$) are often not well-behaved functions of design variables. Bayesian optimization is a strategy that seeks a global optimum of an expensive-to-evaluate function of which little underlying structure is assumed. Here, we model the output of TCAD simulations as such a function and show that Bayesian optimization is capable of exploring the Ge profile design space, providing optimized profiles in as few as 30 simulation iterations.

articleTitle: A D-band Power-Combined Stacked Common-Base Power Amplifier Achieving 20.9 dBm Psat and 24.3 % PAE in a 250-nm InP HBT Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a high-power high-efficiency stacked D-band power amplifier (PA) in a 250-nm HBT technology. The pseudo-differential PA is 2-way power-combined with a power combining network exhibiting a single-transformer footprint and a low loss by reflecting asymmetry leaking to the common mode. The presented PA has a saturated output power of 20.9 dBm and a peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 24.3%. A small-signal gain of $\mathbf{1 4. 2} \mathbf{d B}$ is obtained with a 3-dB bandwidth of 19 GHz.

articleTitle: A Two-stage, Two-way-combined, 220-GHz Power Amplifier With 17.1% PAE in a 250-nm InP HBT Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A 220-GHz power amplifier (PA) in 250-nm Indium Phosphide (InP) is presented achieving a power added efficiency (PAE) of 17.1% at an associated output power of 43 mW. This design leverages common-base heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) with cross-coupling capacitance for higher gain and improved stability. Two stages of gain are realized using pseudo-differential power combining of these cross-coupled cells through low-loss slot-line baluns and the overall PA occupies 230 x 350 um-sq which fits within a phased array pitch at G-band.

articleTitle: Exploring Breakdown Voltage Improvement in 20-nm InGaAs-Channel HEMT-OI with Metallic Back-Gate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We report on a $20-\mathrm{nm}$ gate length Quantum-Well High-Electron-Mobility Transistor (HEMT) on a Silicon Sub strate with an InGaAs channel. A back-gated metallic field-plate, connected to the buffer backside, is used to provide dynamic threshold and breakdown voltages. After calibrating TCAD simulations against experimental results, we explored the possibility of enhancing the transistor breakdown voltage by varying the geometric parameters of the back-gate as well as the cap layer concentration. Our findings indicate that increasing the back-gate length relative to the middle of the front gate can enhance the HEMT breakdown voltage by over 10%. Reducing the cap layer concentration or removing the cap layer, in addition to the presence of the back-gate, can drastically improve both the output conduction and the breakdown voltage by over 1 V compared to the reference. This study opens up the possibility for new analog and RF designs utilizing this back-gate.

articleTitle: Integrated Photonics in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Lithium niobate ($\mathbf{L N}$), an outstanding and versatile material, has influenced our daily life for decades: from enabling high-speed optical communications that form the backbone of the Internet to realizing radio-frequency filtering used in our cell phones. This half-century-old material is currently embracing a revolution in thin-film $\mathbf{L N}$ integrated photonics. The success of manufacturing wafer-scale, high-quality, thin films of LN on insulator, accompanied with breakthroughs in nanofabrication techniques, have made high-performance integrated nanophotonic components possible. With rapid development in the past few years, some of these thin-film LN (TFLN) devices [1], such as optical modulators and nonlinear wavelength converters, have already outperformed their legacy counterparts realized in bulk LN crystals. Furthermore, the nanophotonic integration enabled ultra-low-loss resonators in LN, which unlocked many novel applications such as optical frequency combs and quantum transducers. In this presentation, I will provide an introduction into the field of TFLN with a focus on high-performance electro optical modulators with applications in Telecom, Datacom, test and more.

articleTitle: On the Safe Operating Area of InP HBTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The safe-operating area of an advanced InP HBT technology is studied experimentally using pulsed, DC and RF as well as load-pull measurements. To study the implications of the results on circuit performance, a power amplifier cell is analyzed using HICUM/L2. Safe-operating-area related consequences for circuit design, technology development, compact modeling and device characterization are outlined.

articleTitle: A Low-Noise Amplifier in 130-nm InP HBT with 15.5 dB Gain and Record 5.3 dB Noise-Figure at 212 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present a low-noise amplifier (LNA) in Teledyne $130-\mathrm{nm}$ InP technology, featuring peak 15.6 dB gain and better than 8 dB input return loss over $\mathrm{1 7 0 - 2 5 0 ~ G H z}$. The designed LNA employs a cascade of five common-emitter stages and adopts a design procedure based on the minimum noise measure. The LNA achieves $\mathrm{5. 7 5} \pm \mathrm{0. 4 5} \mathrm{d B}$ noise-figure (NF) in the measurement frequency range of $\mathrm{1 8 0 - 2 1 6 ~ G H z}$. It consumes $0.25 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ die area, including the DC bias pads, and dissipates 7.6 mW of DC power. To the authors’ knowledge, this work demonstrates record NF results at 200 GHz and above for LNAs designed in any bipolar technology.

articleTitle: A Low-Power, High-Swing LDMOS Driver Amplifier for Shuttling Controller in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer Operating at 4 K
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work presents a three-stage, low-power, low-noise, high-voltage (HV) operational amplifier (op-amp) capable of amplifying arbitrary waveforms at cryogenic temperatures to the high-voltage levels necessary to drive electrodes of a quantum processor. Intended for future integration into a larger system on chip (SoC), this HV op-amp would be the final stage of a shuttling controller in a trapped-ion quantum computer (TIQC). The op-amp provides amplified signals from an arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) to trap electrodes to control the shuttling of ions inside the trap. Measurements conducted both at room temperature and at 4 K to prove its functionality. The op-amp is implemented in 130 nm HV bulk CMOS technology offering laterally-diffused metal-oxide semiconductor (LDMOS) transistors. It consumes 7.2 mW from a dual power supply of 4.3 V and 24 V. The DC gain was measured at 4 K to be around 66 dB. With a load of 31 pF, a slew rate of $17 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{\mu}$ s was obtained at a full-scale (FS) output swing of 16 V. Keywords - quantum computing (QC), high-voltage (HV), operational amplifier (op-amp)

articleTitle: Towards 500GHz fMAX 140nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology for 5G/6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Continued advancements in SiGe BiCMOS technology have enabled the design of mmWave integrated circuits to serve various markets, such as automotive radar, 5G and upcoming 6G. As application requirements push to higher frequency bands, further performance improvements are needed. The focus of this paper is to report on work done to improve the RF performance of SiGe HBT devices implemented using both non-selective and selective epitaxial base architectures in a 140 nm BiCMOS technology. The technology development challenges are discussed, along with device results.

articleTitle: A 64Gb/s Si-Photonic Micro-Ring Resonator Transceiver with Co-designed CMOS Driver and TIA for WDM Optical-IO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid-integrated Silicon Photonic (SiPh) transceiver chipsets for the in-package optical I/O. A dual-segment micro-ring modulator (MRM) and co-designed driver is proposed in the transmitter, where the main and pre-emphasis paths are separately optimized for higher aggregated bandwidth. The driver employs an asymmetric inductive peaking to compensate for MRM non-linearity. The receiver employs a cascaded ring resonator (CRR) to achieve high-Q and wide passband filtering for wavelength division multiplexing (WDM). A high-speed CMOS TIA is co-designed with integrated wavelength tuning. Polarization insensitive optical reception is achieved by the 2 D grating coupler and bidirectional input photodetector. Experimental results show the proposed SiPh transmitter achieves 3.2dB ER at $64 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ and could achieve a maximum transmission speed of $70 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s}$. The receiver achieves 64Gb/s speed with 4.5ps RMS jitter at - 7 dBm optical input, where the $\mathbf{R X}$ bit error rate BER reaches $10^{-12}$.

articleTitle: A Biasing Scheme for the Gain Compression Point Optimization of HBT Cascode D-Band LNAs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Cascode amplifiers with a matching network between the common-emitter (CE) and the common-base (CB) HBTs are popular in the sub-THz band for their enhanced gain. The stage is analyzed in this paper with focus on the large-signal behavior. It is first observed that the CE-CB interstage network can push the CB out of the linear class-A regime, limiting the input power at 1 dB gain compression. It is then shown that the issue can be avoided with a suitable biasing scheme, leading to enhanced dynamic range with superior power efficiency. The concept is applied to the design of a D-band LNA in BiCMOS technology. With a quiescent power consumption of 20 mW from 2 V supply, the LNA shows 17.5 dB gain and 5.5 dB NF at 170 GHz. The output-referred 1dB compression point is 4.2dBm with 9% power efficiency at 175 GHz. Compared to previously reported LNAs in the same band, measured results demonstrate a remarkable dynamic range improvement with the the highest power efficiency.

articleTitle: Full Antenna in Package Solution for 100GHz 6G infrastructure, in 140nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper we describe a 64 channel Antenna in Package (AIP) solution, containing 4 16-channel Analog Beam Former (ABF) ICs and 1 Up-Down Converter (UDC) designed and fabricated in a 140nm SiGe BiCMOS in-house Technology. This AIP can be used both for user equipment and as building block in larger phased array antenna panels for 6G infrastructure equipment operating at 100GHz.

articleTitle: A 5.6 dB NF Two-Stage 110 - 125 GHz LNA Gain-Boosted by RC-over-Neutralization for Radar Applications in 28 nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage differential LNA operating at around 120 GHz achieving a measured noise figure of 5.6 dB. We obtain a gain of 6.65 dB per stage by means of the RC-over-neutralization technique. Hence, the LNA exhibits an overall measured gain of 13.3 dB using only two stages and therefore occupies a minimal core area of only $0.03 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. Lossy over-neutralization technique has been used so far mainly for power amplifiers, while in this work we apply it for an LNA. Furthermore, we extend this approach by adding an explicit neutralization resistance, which provides another design degree of freedom, enabling independent choice of $R_{\mathrm{n}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{n}}$ during the physical circuit implementation. We analyze systematically the $R_{\mathrm{n}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{n}}$ values to achieve simultaneously optimal NF and gain. We show that $R_{\mathrm{n}}$ causes only a minimal NF degradation, yet it enables boosting gain per stage. The circuit is realized in 28 nm bulk CMOS process and dissipates only 25.2 mW from a single 0.9 V supply. It achieves in measurement an RF-bandwidth of 15 GHz and $\mathrm{IP}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}$ linearity of -17.3 dBm. The presented two-stage LNA can be useful for area saving in D-band receivers.

articleTitle: W-band GaN Resistive FET I-Q Mixer MMICs with Low Conversion Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a single-balanced resistive FET (RFET) MMIC downconvert mixers using HRL Laboratories 40nm T3 GaN HEMT process operating in a single-ended and I-Q modes. MMIC size is 2.5mm X 2.5mm. The mixer operates at W-band with the RF frequency ranging from 92-96 GHz and Local Oscillator (LO) frequency from 86-95 GHz. The Conversion Loss (CL) measured in an image reject mode is 8dB across the band, P1dB is >20.3dBm and the IIP3 is 28dBm. The LO-RF isolation is in the 13dB range. I-Q phase imbalance is 8 degrees on average. To our knowledge, this is the lowest CL achieved at W-band for a GaN RFET Mixer.

articleTitle: 10-GSymbols/s Supply Modulated 250-GHz SiGe HBT Transmitter RF Front-End with 6.8-dBm Peak Modulated Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A 250-GHz SiGe HBT (fT and $\mathrm{f}_{\text {max }}$ of $\mathbf{3 0 0} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and 450 GHz) transmitter RF front-end using supply modulation at 10GSymbols/s along with a 16-customized-APSK (APSK ${ }_{c}$) constellation is used to generate instrumentation limited 40-Gbps signals with a peak modulated power of 6.8 dBm and an EVM of -18.9 dB, while consuming $\sim 1 W$ of DC power. The peak modulated output power and efficiency for the average modulated power generation of the transmitter RF front-end is 3 X and 2.3 X higher than when conventional QAM modulation with a backoff is employed. The $6.8-\mathrm{dBm}$ peak modulated power is the highest among the reported in literature.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Low Phase Noise Broadband Amplifier in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper reports on a low phase noise broadband amplifier based on distributed amplification (DA) employing travelling-wave architecture. We introduce a design methodology for achieving low phase noise in travelling-wave amplifier (TWA) by integrating appropriate design principles and biasing conditions. The influence of various circuit parameters on flicker (1/f) noise characteristics are investigated, aiming to reduce baseband 1/f noise and its upconversion to the carrier frequency. Using this approach, we designed a three-section TWA that exhibits a gain of 10 dB and a 3 dB bandwidth of around 47 GHz occupying an active chip area of 0.69 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Output referred 1 dB compression point (OP1dB) of 12dBm is demonstrated using large signal measurements. Compared against the state of art, our presented wideband amplifier achieves superior phase noise performance of -169 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset frequency for a 10 GHz signal in SiGe BiCMOS technology.

articleTitle: Single-Chip 30 GHz SiGe Sub-Sampling PLL with 28.3 fs Jitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We demonstrate a phase locked loop (PLL) in a 45 nm PDSOI process with SiGe heterojunction bipolar devices (HBTs). The PLL has an output frequency centered around 30 GHz and exhibits low jitter and in-band phase noise. Measurements demonstrate -100.9 / -116.6 / -126.9 dBc/Hz phase noise at 1 kHz / 1 MHz / 10 MHz offsets, with integrated jitter of 28.3 fs (rms). It combines the far-out low phase noise performance of a SiGe HBT LC-VCO with a sub-sampling loop that significantly reduces the in-band noise contribution from loop filter components. The 45 nm PDSOI FETs enable sub-sampling bandwidth over 30 GHz. The loop filter features a wide degree of tunability, enabling optimization of in-band and far-out phase noise.

articleTitle: The Design of Wideband LNAs in 45nm SiGe BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work presents the design of two low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) with variations in the second amplification stage to study trade-offs in gain, bandwidth, and linearity. Implemented in a 45 nm SiGe BiCMOS process, the two designs achieved wideband gains (S21) from 16.2-55.0 GHz and 11.1-32.1 GHz with simultaneous broadband input matching (S11) bandwidths of 26.1-55.0 GHz and 11.6-33.4 GHz, respectively. The LNAs obtain a minimum noise figure (NF) of 3.4 dB and 2.3 dB, peak gains of 13.1 dB and 19.9 dB, and maximum IIP3s of 5.7 dBm and -4.7 dBm while using 18.0 mW and 14.4 mW of power from a 1.5 V supply. These performance metrics enable record FoM performance when compared to both state-of-the-art CMOS and SiGe LNA designs.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band SiGe:C Power Amplifier with 24.8 dBm Output Power and 35.6% Peak PAE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband power amplifier for the $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{u}}$-Band. The architecture of the single PA cell is a fully differential topology. For full characterization of the differential topology and its benefits additional PAs with passive power combining and baluns are also investigated. The PAs are fabricated in Infineon’s BiCMOS production technology B11HFC which offers HBTs with an $f_{\mathrm{T}}$ of 250 GHz and $f_{\max }$ of 370 GHz. The single PA cell achieves a peak output power of 24.8 dBm and a peak PAE of 35.6% at 13 GHz. The quiescent current of the single PA-cell is 181 mA from a single 3.3V supply.

articleTitle: A Sub-Sampling 35GHz PLL in 45nm PDSOI BiCMOS with 37fs Integrated Jitter and a FoM of -252dB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a $34-35 \mathrm{GHz}$ integer-N sub-sampling phase-locked loop (PLL) in a 45nm PDSOI BiCMOS ($0.1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ SiGe HBT integrated with 45 nm PDSOI) technology. This monolithic integration takes full advantage of SiGe HBT’s low noise and PDSOI’s low power consumption characteristics. The designed and implemented PLL is tested with a low phase noise of $-123.69 \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{Hz}$ at 1 MHz offset and an integrated RMS jitter of 37fs. While dissipating 63mW, it realizes a jitter FoM of -250.7dB (FLL on) and -252.2dB (FLL off).

articleTitle: Load-Modulated Balanced Amplifiers for Next-G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This article presents an overview of the recent advances in load-modulated balanced amplifier (LMBA), which has been a highly popular topic in RF research. The theory and design equations are revisited for different types of couplers, which were typically not distinguished in existing literature. Moreover, the design methodology is re-developed based on signal-flow analysis of individual balanced amplifier (BA) and control amplifier (CA) paths, indicating the intrinsic wideband nature of LMBA. Furthermore, LMBA design space are expanded with various modes showing highly desirable features for emerging wireless applications, including power back-off (PBO) range, linearity and insensitivity to load (antenna) impedance variations. A few realistic design examples are experimentally demonstrated to showcase the advantages of LMBA over state-of-the-art and the promising potential for next-G communications.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Zero Ω Transmission Line Analysis and Design at W-Band and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: At G-band and beyond, DC feeding circuits pose significant challenges. Circuit elements shrink in size as frequencies increase and for that reason traditional methods of delivering DC power using transmission lines (TLs) encounter limitations, the $\lambda / 4$ line length is too short and an electrical length larger than $\lambda / 2$ presents high losses. In response to the challenges outlined above, this work introduces a novel low ohmic transmission line design methodology (zero- $\Omega$ TL), underpinned by rigorous mathematical analysis. This methodology provides a structured and systematic approach to designing the zero- $\Omega$ TL by analyzing the characteristic impedance of individual lines -an approach that saves computation time and effort.

Author Keywords: DC power supply and ideal RF short circuit

articleTitle: Broadband Linear Drivers for 800G/1.6T Energy Efficient Optical Links
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work presents the design of a uniform distributed amplifier (LDHP) and a tapered distributed amplifier (LDHE) for linear-drive pluggable optical (LPO) transmitters. The drivers are implemented in the GlobalFoundries $\mathbf{9 H P +}$ 90-nm SiGe BiCMOS process. LDHP has $\mathbf{3. 1 \%}$ total harmonic distortion for 4 Vppd swing up to 22 GHz and achieves 100 GBd PAM-8 with an efficiency of $3.32 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$. LDHE utilizes tapered output transmission line to obtain good efficiency and linearity and achieves 120 GBd PAM-4 at $2.52 \mathrm{pJ} / \mathrm{bit}$. The drivers are targeted for 800 Gbps and 1.6 Tbps optical links.

articleTitle: Characterization of ScAlN/GaN Toward Electronic Device Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Scandium Aluminum Nitride (ScAIN) is an attractive material as a barrier layer of GaN HEMTs owing to its ultrawide bandgap, strong polarization and ferroelectric. In the paper, the recent progress in the characterization of ScAlN/GaN heterostructure prepared by low-temperature sputtering method is presented. Structural and optical properties of epitaxial pseudomorphic ScAIN with Sc compositions of 6,10 and 14% on GaN are investigated by AFM, XRD and spectroscopic ellipsometry. Consistent thicknesses of $\mathbf{\sim 2 0} \mathbf{~ n m}$ were obtained by XRD and spectroscopic ellipsometry. Dielectric function and optical bandgap are determined.

articleTitle: High Temperature Annealing induced recovery of Hot-Carrier degradation in High Performance NPN SiGe HBTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We investigate the possibility of any spontaneous recovery of the hot-carrier injection (HCI) induced degradation in NPN SiGe HBTs as well as the recovery mechanism of the hot carrier damage when the SiGe HBTs are subjected to a high temperature annealing (bake) environment. In our study, devices were HCI stressed under the forward-active/mixed mode as well as the reverse emitter-base (EB) mode and were subsequently stored unbiased under room temperature for ten years. Characterization of these devices at the end of the ten-year storing period showed no recovery of the HCI damage. On the other hand, we observed significant levels of recovery when we thermally cured these same devices even at a low anneal temperature of $180^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The recovery was characterized as a function of the anneal temperature, the annealing time duration and the pre-anneal level of HCI damage. The measured recovery kinetics for the devices that were stressed under the forward-active/mixed mode and those that were stressed under the reverse EB mode are, within the experimental uncertainty, the same, suggesting that the same type of defects are activated during stress in both cases. The recovery rate exhibits Arrhenius behavior, and the extracted activation energy values for the forward-active/mixed mode and reverse EB mode stressed and attributed to the re-passivation of Si dangling bonds by hydrogen atoms.

articleTitle: Design of a Terahertz InP HBT Quadrupler and Silicon Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work details the design and characterization of a terahertz (THz) frequency quadrupler in a 250 nm Indium Phosphide (InP) heterojunction bipolar transistor technology (HBT) $\left(f_{t} / f_{\text {max }} 350 / 600 \mathrm{GHz}\right)$ with output at 580 GHz. The design uses coupled lines to optimize loss, matching and output power. Next, this work first details the fabrication of a custom silicon interposer than can be used on integrated circuits with soft dielectrics that are difficult to reliably wirebond to. Compared to prior art, we describe a single structure that can be used to interface the die to a PCB for low speed connections. This technique does not require additional processing like recessing in a newer structure, and can be adapted to fit any configuration of pads. The technique is hence amenable to package radio-frequency integrated circuit (RFIC) designs that include on-chip inductors, and that need careful consideration to the environment in the vicinity of the inductors. The intervening structure is also shorter compared to conventional wirebonds. This interposer technique has the potential to be further extended to provide reliable connections at radio frequency (RF), and is the topic of current research. The interposer detailed is used to provide bias connections to the chip. Quadrupler S-parameter and large signal characterization results, and correlation with simulations are discussed next.

articleTitle: TCAD for Circuits and Systems: Process Emulation, Parasitics Extraction, Self-Heating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present TCAD-based methodologies that go beyond process and device simulations of single transistors. We show that TCAD solvers can be used as effective tools to resolve the intricacies of current and future technology nodes that are otherwise difficult to access using EDA-level methods alone.

articleTitle: Large-Signal Modeling of a 50 nm mHEMT Incorporating a Physical Impact-Ionization Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper, investigations on the gate-current of 50 nm metamorphic HEMTs (mHEMT) are performed, where evidences on impact ionization are observed. An accurate fit for different device sizes was obtained using a physical model for its induced gate-current, suggesting further indications that the observed phenomena are related to impact ionization. An empirical large-signal model a 50 nm gate-lenght mHEMT incorporating the physical model is presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Design kit development on a 300mm GaN-on-Si demonstration platform with integrated Si pMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Gallium Nitride electronics will provide impactful efficiency and size benefits to many industries. But to unleash its full potential, a systems approach is necessary with tight integration of complementary low-voltage devices for logic, driver and bias blocks alongside performant high-voltage devices and appropriate passives, all in a unified design kit. This work describes Intel’s on-going progress with such a platform for 300 mm R&D prototyping of GaN systems, including a full-featured backend, an embrace of industry-standard compact models, design considerations for integration of E-mode Gallium Nitride MOSHEMTs with Si pMOSFETs, and further devices in development to complete the designer’s toolkit.

articleTitle: On the Emitter Back-Injection Current in Advanced SiGe HBTs at Cryogenic Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Designing current amplifiers at cryogenic temperatures requires an accurate description of the current gain of HBTs, which is impacted by the forward base current injected back into the emitter. Its bias dependence for a given temperature so far has been modeled by a diode equation with an empirically modeled ideality factor $m_{\mathrm {{B E}}}$ for describing its experimentally observed strong temperature dependence. This work analyzes different carrier statistics and transport mechanisms and provides the most likely physical origin for the observed strong increase of $m_{\mathrm {{B E}}}$ at cryogenic temperatures.

articleTitle: Trends in Millimeter-Wave and THz Test Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This brief survey looks at some current challenges and advances in millimeter-wave and THz test equipment. In particular, spectral purity of mm-wave signal sources and downconverters is addressed, both at full power and in power-sweeping configurations. Higher-power VNA measurement capabilities are introduced. New advances in millimeter-wave noise measurements and wideband signal analysis are also described.

articleTitle: 300-GHz 160-Gb/s InP-HEMT Wireless Front-End With Fully Differential Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a 300-GHz-band 160-Gb/s fully differential integrated transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) front-end (FE) that is based on our in-house $60-\mathrm{nm}$ InP high-electron mobility transistor (InP-HEMT) technology. To integrate the RF power amplifier (PA) and mixer while avoiding RF PA saturation caused by the mixer’s LO leakage (LOL), the proposed fully differential $F E$ architecture uses a double-balanced mixer, high common-mode rejection differential amplifier, and LO phase inverter (LOPI). The TX and RX modules achieve a conversion gain (CG) of above 5 dB over wide bandwidths of 35 and 56 GHz, respectively. We successfully demonstrated 16QAM $160-\mathrm{Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ back-to-back data transmission using the proposed FE. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the highest reported data rate achieved with a 300-GHz-band FE.

articleTitle: A compact low-loss Ku-Band 90° Hybrid Coupler for Front-End Modules in 45 nm SOI CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated 90° hybrid coupler chip designed for the frequency range of $12-16 \mathrm{GHz}$, intended for high-power backhaul applications. We show that a simplified equivalent circuit model can be used for accurate dimensioning of the coupler. The analytical model demonstrates a very good correlation with an electromagnetic field simulation and 4-port measurement results. The measured amplitude and phase imbalances in the desired frequency range are $\mathbf{0. 7 5} \mathrm{dB}$ and $89.5^{\circ} \pm 0.5^{\circ}$, respectively. The chip is implemented using GlobalFoundries 45RFE technology and occupies an area of $0.34 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$, including pads.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Model Verification and Analysis of Unmatched Multi-Finger HBT Cells at 220 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this paper we verify the small-signal performance and simulation accuracy of two common-emitter (CE) and one common-base (CB) multi-finger heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) cells used in power amplifier designs at 220 GHz. We first verify the accuracy of the manifold simulation, the structure connecting multiple HBTs together, using passive structures that comprise the manifold before verifying the accuracy of the single-finger model and the four-finger cell simulation. We find that the discrepancies between simulation and measurement of the four-finger cell tends to be the same as or lower than the discrepancies in the single-finger device from140 - 230 GHz. The simulation accurately predicts the gain of all cells and the reflection coefficients of the CB cell. However, there are discrepancies between simulated and measured reflection coefficients of both CE cells, with a difference in linear magnitude greater than 0.1, and discrepancies with the measured stability factor of the CB cell.

articleTitle: Ka-Band MMIC Implementation of a Load-Modulating Loop Combiner Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This letter presents a MMIC implementation of the Load-Modulating Loop Combiner (LMLC) power amplifier (PA) architecture for Ka-band operation. This architecture incorporates elements of a feed-forward amplifier topology and the Doherty power amplifier to provide load modulation operation and improved linearity performance. A GaN MMIC operating at 28 GHz was designed and measured. The device presented in this work operates with a peak output power of 33.4 dBm and 33.7% peak PAE. Modulated measurements with a 100 MHz LTE signal are also presented.

articleTitle: A 7.7-mW DC-to-62 GHz Ultra-Wideband Low-Noise Amplifier with ±2.1 ps Group Delay Variation and 3.3 dB NF in 0.13-μm SiGe:C BiCMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A low-power ultra-wideband (UWB) low-noise amplifier (LNA) implemented in a $0.13 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ SiGe:C BiCMOS technology with $300 / 500 \mathrm{GHz} f_{\mathrm{T}} / f_{\max }$ is presented. The LNA achieves a measured DC gain of 11.2 dB with a 3 dB bandwidth $\left(\mathrm{BW}_{3 \mathrm{~dB}}\right)$ from DC to $\mathbf{6 2} \mathbf{~ G H z}$ and a noise figure (NF) of $\lt3.5 \mathrm{~dB}$ while consuming only 7.7 mW. The measured $\mathrm{IP}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}} / \mathrm{OP}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}$ at 20 GHz and 40 GHz is $-11 /-1 \mathrm{dBm}$ and $-12.5 /-2.4 \mathrm{dBm}$, respectively. In addition, the measured average group delay (GD) is 6.1 ps with a corresponding GD variation $(\Delta \tau)$ of ±2.1ps within the $\mathrm{BW}_{3 \mathrm{~dB}}$, demonstrating an excellent phase linearity. The overall chip area is $300 \mu \mathrm{~m} \times 310 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this general-purpose UWB LNA achieves the best FoMs with a very low power consumption and an excellent NF among prior published silicon-based wideband amplifiers for both wireless and wireline applications to date.

articleTitle: A 130-GHz Bandwidth 61-dBOhm Variable-Gain Differential Linear TIA in a 130-nm SiGe:C BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A differential linear transimpedance amplifier (TIA) implemented in a 130-nm SiGe:C BiCMOS technology with $f_{\text {T}} / f_{\text {max }}$ of $350 / 450 ~\mathrm{GHz}$ is presented which features a bandwidth of $130 ~\mathrm{GHz}, ~61 ~\mathrm{dBOhm}$ maximum transimpedance (TI) gain and 20-dB gain variability while dissipating 170 mW of DC power. The measured total harmonic distortion (THD) in the maximum gain setting is below 5% for a 750 mVppd output swing and an input current of 600 uApp. To the best of the author’s knowledge, the presented design shows the highest bandwidth among integrated TIAs, while simultaneously demonstrating comparable TI gain, noise characteristics, linearity and DC power consumption compared to state-of-the-art designs.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage 24 Gb/s 8:1 Cryogenic Multiplexer for Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work presents a single-stage 8:1 current mode logic (CML) multiplexer (MUX) with integrated active baluns at the inputs within the block and clock distribution network with $\mathbf{1 2. 5 \%}$ duty cycle clock generation. It is intended for constructing a highly integrated cryogenic high-speed system-on-chip (SoC) with a return-to-zero converter and a current buffer intended to drive Josephson Arbitrary Waveform Synthesizers (JAWS). Usually, 8:1 MUX consists of seven 2:1 MUX gates and three clock signals at different frequencies. This results in increased power consumption and a complex clock distribution. The proposed single-stage 8:1 MUX solution simplifies system realization. The chip is realized in a $0.13 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ BiCMOS process. The chip was measured at data rates from $800 \mathrm{Mb} / \mathrm{s}$ up to 24 $\mathrm{Gb} / \mathrm{s}$ with a ±123mV single-ended voltage swing on a $50 \Omega$ load at room temperature (RT). The core chip area is $0.132 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ and DC consumption is 224 mW. To author’s knowledge this is the first single-stage 8:1 MUX for driving JAWS measured at 16 K.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Physical ASM-HEMT Model Using a Neural Network-Based Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This work reports the first hybrid physical ASMHEMT model in a $150-\mathrm{nm}$ GaN technology. The standard ASM-HEMT model is further enhanced by logically introducing bias-dependent capacitance and resistance model parameters to compensate for the missing physical behavior not captured by the model. This adaptation enhances the fitting of the device’s junction capacitances and intrinsic resistances across a wide range of bias conditions (from 15 to $500 \mathrm{~mA} / \mathrm{mm}$), proving particularly beneficial for non-standard or emerging device designs. To comprehensively evaluate the large-signal accuracy of the hybrid ASM-HEMT model, we provide large-signal data in the form of X-parameters and dynamic load lines, which result in good agreement to demonstrate the efficacy of adopting a hybrid physical modeling methodology.

articleTitle: The Effect of Base Doping Profile on Horizontal Current Bipolar Transistor’s (HCBT) Beta Recovery at Cryogenic Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: It has been recently demonstrated that horizontal current bipolar transistor (HCBT) shows a recovery of DC current gain $(\beta)$ at cryogenic temperatures (CT) below $\sim 90 \mathrm{~K}$, a unique property among the silicon bipolar transistors. This effect can be explained by the interplay between incomplete ionization (II) of the acceptors in the base and bandgap narrowing (BGN) in the emitter in a specific range of HCBT doping profiles. To better understand the critical role of base doping parameters on $\beta$ recovery at CT, the HCBT with a lower-doped-collector (HCBT 2) was compared to the previously characterized HCBT with an nwell collector (HCBT 1). HCBT 2 also exhibits a $\beta$ recovery at CT, although less prominent than in the case of HCBT 1. HCBT 2 reaches a minimum peak $\beta$ at $\sim 70 \mathrm{~K}$ of 25, whereas HCBT 1’s minimum $\beta$ of 31 is at a higher temperature of $\sim \mathbf{9 0} \mathrm{K}$. Moreover, the $\beta$ recovery at CT of HCBT 2 reaches 37, which is lower than HCBT 1’s $\beta$ of 64 at 20 K. Calibrated TCAD simulations of equivalent BJT structures show that small relative differences in the base doping profile near Mott transition limit can have a significant impact on the cryogenic performance of the device. The demonstrated properties of both devices can enable the implementation of cryogenic circuits in HCBT BiCMOS technology.

articleTitle: Practical Dimensions of Contemporary GaN Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of current GaN device modeling techniques along with recent advances implanted in practical and commercially available solutions. The empirical and physics-based compact models are reviewed with focus on enhanced versions of the Angelov and ASM-HEMT models. Enhancements of the standard ASM-HEMT model with improved charge model and advanced trap modeling are discussed. Improved large-signal validation results are shown. Furthermore, practical error metrics for various model validations are presented to provide a quantitative evaluation of the accuracy of nonlinear models. Advanced nonlinear embedding model-based PA design approach is also discussed.

articleTitle: Practical Simulation and Test Strategies for Advanced Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper explores common challenges encountered during electrical test or simulation of advanced heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs), including thermal runaway, collector-base avalanche, pinch-in, and stress-induced degradation (aging). Insight into each effect is presented in the context of typical test procedures used during device evaluation. The benefits and pitfalls of various biasing schemes are discussed in order to identify practical approaches to broad-bias characterization for both DC and AC test.

articleTitle: A D-band SiGe Subharmonic Downconverter with Dynamic Conversion Gain and Fixed Input Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: A fourth subharmonic downconverter operates with a bandwidth of 123-158 GHz and incorporates bias feedback to control the conversion gain over a large LO power range. A push-pull frequency multiplier achieves a high multiplication factor (X4) without sacrificing the additional area or power of a cascaded multiplier chain. Wide bandwidth is achieved by use of a sub-quarter-wavelength (SQWL) balun and an inductivelypeaked transimpedance amplifier (TIA). The downconverter is realized in a 90-nm SiGe BiCMOS technology and has a peak conversion gain 7.5 dB at 155 GHz with -5 dBm of LO power at 35 GHz while consuming a maximum 55 mW of DC power and 0.196 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of area. The minimum 1-dB input compression power (P1dB) at 155 GHz is -15 dBm. Compared to earlier work, this paper demonstrates a higher LO multiplication factor with lower LO power requirements and over 20 dB of dynamic gain control while having the same peak power consumption and a 1.9 dB/dB conversion gain to LO power trade-off.

articleTitle: Characterization and Large-Signal Modeling of 4-Pole Backgated InGaAs HEMT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents, for the first time, the electrical measurements, characterization, and large-signal modeling of a backgated 4-pole, 20 nm InGaAs HEMT device. The primary objective of this work is to characterize and model the influence of varying backgate voltages on device performance. A robust empirical large-signal model that accurately captures the impact of these voltage variations on the device characteristics is developed. This model is constructed by identifying the parameters directly affected by the backgate voltage and formulating analytical equations to describe this dependency. By manipulating the backgate voltage to attain a positive threshold voltage, these models can be used to design mixed-signal circuits with digital logic capabilities.

articleTitle: ASM-GaN Model for Resistive Mixer Applications at D-Band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper reports on the large-signal modeling of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility-transistors. The physicsbased model parameters of the Advanced SPICE Model are used to accurately reproduce the large-signal behavior of different gate length GaN HEMTs even with varying gate-drain and gatesource ledges focusing on passive mixer applications at D-band frequencies (110 - 170 GHz). Dedicated models for 70 nm GaN HEMTs and 100 nm GaN HEMTs with different ledge distances are presented. All models show an excellent agreement with dc and S-parameter measurements of single HEMT devices up to 150 GHz. Furthermore, the 100 nm GaN HEMT model is verified based on an existing resistive D-band mixer MMIC. This shows that the model offers the option to analyze trends in circuit performance (e.g. linearity) when key technology parameters such as the gate length are varied.

articleTitle: Using Pulsed-Mode Measurements of SiGe HBTs for Non-Destructive, Improved RF-SOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present a new approach for exploring the underlying reliability physics of SiGe HBTs, and define a new, application-relevant safe-operating area (SOA) of devices by implementing pulsed-voltage measurements. Compared to DC measurements, pulsed-mode measurements have the advantage of being non-destructive, and can be used to decouple self-heating and impact ionization to predict hard failure under large RF swings. In the present work, one of the conventional DC SOA criteria is explored as a function of pulse-width in state-of-the-art SiGe HBTs. The collector-current density ($J_{C}$) doubles at a later voltage under pulsed conditions vs. DC, resulting in an additional SOA margin of 0.8 V at peak-$f_{T}$ quiescent current. Load-pull measurements show that the devices experience hard failure at about the same bias as the new pulsed-mode SOA definition for the shortest measured pulse-width (160 ns). Load lines overlaid with the pulsed-SOA definition demonstrate that the device experiences hard failure when the RF current swing and voltage are outside the pulsed-mode SOA boundary. These results demonstrate pulsed-mode measurements as a new and useful tool wherein pulsed width can be adjusted to improve the correlation between measurements of the SOA and hard failure under application-relevant RF operating conditions. Furthermore, pulsed-mode SOA can be measured using forced voltage between the base and the emitter, often preferred for power amplifiers, which allows designers to explore more aggressive operational bias conditions that provide circuit peRFormance advantages while remaining robust to damage.

articleTitle: A Direct Digital Synthesizer-Based Arbitrary Waveform Generator for Envelope Modulation in Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer Operating at 4K
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents an Arbitrary Waveform Generator (AWG) based on a Direct Digital Synthesizer (DDS) with a sub-Hz frequency resolution. The proposed circuit generates a low-frequency arbitrary signal used for amplitude modulation of a microwave (MW) carrier signal, required for qubit entanglement operations with an enhanced gate fidelity in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Computer (TIQC). This is realized by utilizing a DDS as a custom waveform generator. The proposed mixed-signal circuit operates at a 2.5 V analog and 1.5 V digital supply and dissipates $52 \mu \mathrm{~W} / \mathrm{MHz}$. The chip was measured from 4 K to 297 K and achieves a SFDR of $\mathbf{4 2} \mathbf{~ d B c}$. The design is fabricated in Infineon’s $\mathbf{0. 1 3} \mu \mathrm{m}$ SiGe BiCMOS technology and has a core area of $0.45 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first reported AWG for amplitude envelope modulation in trapped-ion quantum computer application.

articleTitle: High-Temperature Stability Base Ohmic Contacts for InP/GaAsSb DHBTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In today’s telecommunications landscape, the need for transistors capable of efficiently handling high power levels at elevated frequencies is paramount. However, these demands present significant hurdles, particularly concerning transistor reliability when devices are required to operate at or near their peak performance levels. In this context, the thermal stability of ohmic contacts in InP/GaAsSb DHBs has to be investigated and improved. We investigated the stability of several ohmic contact stacks on $\boldsymbol{p}$-doped GaAsSb in terms of their resistivity and stability of RF performance of InP/GaAsSb DHBTs subjected to sequential high-temperature annealing isochronal cycles. A Pt/Ir/Pt/Au stack shows the lowest resistance, the highest $f_{\text {max }}$ and little to no performance degradation when devices are annealed up to $350^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. TLM contact resistance measurements do not accurately reflect actual RF performance levels.

articleTitle: 802 Gbps Coherent Optical Sub-Assembly (COSA) based on a Coupling Modulated Silicon Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: We present a coherent optical sub-assembly (COSA) consisting of a silicon ring resonator-based, dual-polarization I/Q coupling modulator and integrated custom silicon germanium (SiGe) drivers. We demonstrate 78-km 802.6-Gbps transmission with 90-GBaud PS-64-QAM modulation.

articleTitle: Performance Limitations of GaN HEMTs with Quaternary InAlGaN and ScAlGaN Barrier Layers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Quaternary alloys such as InAlGaN and ScAlGaN are promising barrier materials for GaN-based advanced high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) due to the higher achievable two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) densities compared to conventional AIGaN barriers. In this work, we analyze the 2DEG density, mobility, on-resistance and transconductance of InAIGaN and ScAIGaN barrier HEMTs using a comprehensive in-house modeling framework, and validate our results with available experimental data for a lattice-matched InAIGaN/AIN/GaN HEMT. We explore the dependence of 2DEG density and mobility on barrier In/Sc-content and Al-content, and obtain an on-resistance below $90 \Omega / \square$ for the ScAIGaN barrier HEMT at Sc-contents below 0.18 and Al-contents above 0.78. We also find that a lattice-matched ScAIGaN barrier device achieves a 2DEG density higher by a factor of 3 at zero gate bias compared to the InAIGaN reference device. This means that a thinner ScAlGaN barrier can be utilized to obtain the same threshold voltage, resulting in a transconductance higher by a factor of 1.78 at an overdrive voltage of 4 V. The study gives insight into the physical mechanisms governing the analyzed figures of merit and provides guidelines for the design of future quaternary barrier HEMTs.

articleTitle: Ka-Band, Reactively Matched Non-Uniform Distributed Power Amplifier MMICs in GaN-on-SiC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The design and measured performance of two high power, Ka-Band GaN MMIC PAs combining non-uniform distributed driving stages with reactively matched output stages are presented. The combination of these circuit topologies achieves a middle ground in performance in terms of bandwidth and efficiency between each topology purely on its own. The two designs achieve 6 W and 15 W of output power with associated PAEs of 16% on average across $30-40 \mathrm{GHz}$ and $28-40 \mathrm{GHz}$ bands, respectively. This paper describes some of the important design considerations at the interface between the distributed and reactively matched stages, while showing state-of-the-art results.

articleTitle: A Q-band Phased-Array Transmit Beamformer in 45 nm CMOS SOI for SATCOM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents a high-gain, high-efficiency phased-array transmit (TX) beamformer chip in a 45-nm RFSOI process for SATCOM phased-array. The beamformer employing a active vector modulated phase shifter and a three-stacked-FETs power amplifier with neutralization, result in high linearity and low power consumption. The measured gain is 25.2 to 28.6 dB of 17.1-18.5 dBm and satuated output power $\left(P_{s a t}\right)$ from 19.5-20.4 dBm, repectively. A peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 24.9% at 39.5 GHz is achieved. The measured root-mean squared (RMS) gain error and phase error are below 0.45 dB and 3 degrees,respectively. The beamformer occupies $1.4 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$ including pads and consumes 225 mW DC power. This work achieves state-of-the-art linearity and efficiency for Q-band SATCOM transmit (TX) phased-array systems.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency High-Conversion-Ratio Power Delivery Circuits for Computing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: With growing demands for 48V-to-1V voltage conversions in computing applications, different topologies of hybrid DC-DC converters were recently reported to explore single-step voltage conversion. This paper reviews and analyzes the features of state-of-the-art hybrid DC-DC converter topologies. Different design insights are given for optimizing the power efficiency of hybrid DC-DC converters. These help researchers develop new innovative hybrid DC-DC converters.

articleTitle: A Versatile 55-nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology for Wired, Wireless, and Satcom Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper presents how the BiCMOS055X technology from STMicroelectronics is defined to serve wired, wireless, and satcom applications with a versatile competitive offer. Technology content is described and differences with the previous generation are highlighted. Performances of all the devices (active and passive) are reviewed, including the SiGe HBT reliability. The design platform offers, and related qualification strategy are also discussed.

articleTitle: III-V Semiconductors in Commercial Communication Satellite Payloads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: There is a need for high performance, high reliability RF electronics (typically referred to as “the payload”) in Commercial Communications Satellites. For these applications, it is required to supply radiation hardened electronics to survive the harsh environment of space while also providing the demanding performance required to meet the payload’s mission. To this end the use of III-V semiconductor technologies has enabled many of these missions. This paper will provide an understanding of what are commercial communications satellites and their payload architectures. This will provide insight into their need for III-V RF active semiconductors. A brief history of communication satellites will be given to allow an understanding of the motivations for using III-V technology, a look at some present requirements will be given to show the state of this technology in this application, and a view of the future usage for this technology will be presented.

articleTitle: Diamond-BN Heterojunctions for High Power Devices: The Ultimate HEMT?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This review explores the properties of diamond and boron nitride as a promising materials combination for high electron mobility transistors, HEMTs. These ultra-wide bandgap materials exhibit excellent electronic properties as well as high thermal conductivity for superior heat dissipation. The lattice mismatch between cubic boron nitride (c-BN) and diamond is $\sim \mathbf{1. 4 \%}$ allowing for the epitaxial growth of heterojunction devices. However, to demonstrate a viable c-BN/diamond HEMT technology a number of significant challenges remain, including: the epitaxial growth of single crystal heterojunctions on large area substrates; control of phosphorus dopant incorporation for n-type channels; and achieving low specific contact resistance to source and drain regions. There has been recent progress towards achieving these goals, paving the way for a new generation of high-power electronic devices for DC and RF applications.

articleTitle: 300-GHz-Band InP HBT Power Amplifier and InP-CMOS Hybrid Phased-Array Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: In this invited paper, we introduce a 300-GHz-band power amplifier (PA) IC and module designed and fabricated in 250-nm InP DHBT technology and a 300-GHz-band InP-CMOS hybrid phased array transmitter for 6G. Our PA module achieved a maximum gain of 30 dB around 260 GHz and maintained over 20 dB within a range from 220 to 310 GHz. It also achieved a saturation power of $9 \mathbf{~ d B m}$ at 270 GHz and demonstrated point-to-point wireless data transmission with a data rate of 100 Gbps at a distance of 40 m. Our phased array transmitter, in which four InP-HBT PA ICs and CMOS ICs containing mixers and control functions are integrated onto the same printed circuit board, achieved a maximum EIRP of $\mathbf{8. 4 ~ d B m}$ and steering range of 36° and successfully demonstrated wireless data transmission of up to 30 Gbps over a distance of 50 cm with beam steering.

articleTitle: N-Path Mixers Beyond CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: N-path mixers, while long known, have seen rapid growth in popularity with the advent of deeply scaled silicon CMOS. This popularity results from these mixers’ unusual filtering properties, extremely high out-of-band linearity, and surprisingly low noise. Here we discuss why scaled CMOS has been the primary technology used when implementing N -path mixers that enabling of these properties, and then how recent advances in circuit topologies allow these circuits to be mapped into other transistor technologies such as GaAs and GaN HEMTs or HBTs, with potentially superior performance.

articleTitle: SiGe and CMOS Technologies for Wireless PA Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: The paper reviews SiGe and CMOS based designs for different power amplifier applications including WiFi, 5G FR2 (mm-wave from $\mathbf{2 4}-\mathbf{7 1 G H z}$) and Autoradar including 140 GHz. The specific system requirements and design approaches are discussed and then recent results in SiGe BiCMOS, planar FETs, FDSOI and Finfets are compared. CMOS based PA designs are typically more cost effective for the same performance level. The pros and cons of different design approaches and technologies used are presented. Technology and design considerations which impact the total estimated cost are also discussed.

articleTitle: A Family of Physics-Based Models for Monolithic GaN Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: This paper provides a brief overview of the family of physics-based MIT Virtual-source Gallium-nitride (MVSG) compact models, including those for Gallium-nitride (GaN) based transistors, multi-channel Schottky diodes, and transmission line (TLM) structures with nonlinear resistance. A coherent model formulation has been adopted across these devices through a modular approach using a universal set of basic modules. We will introduce the the model formulation and the basic modules with the explanation of underlining device phyiscs. Various features, including those non-linear effects critical for GaN applications, such as trapping, self heating, will also be explained and demonstrated. Given its accuracy, scalability and flexibility, this coherent family of physics-based GaN device compact models provide a solid foundation for the development of Process Design Kit for monolithic GaN technology.

articleTitle: An Overview of SiC High-Voltage Power Devices and High-Temperature ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) is one of the ideal semiconductor materials suitable for high-voltage power devices and high-temperature ICs. Although SiC power MOSFETs have been commercialized, the performance is still far from the material limit. MOS-Hall effect measurements and theoretical study revealed that the low electron mobility in n-channel MOSFETs is ascribed to strong Coulomb scattering by trapped electrons. By minimizing thermal oxidation, two-fold improvement of mobility was achieved. The mobility of SiC pchannel MOSFETs is relatively high (approximately $30 \mathrm{~cm}^{2} / \mathrm{Vs}$ on the non-polar face), indicating a potential SiC FinFET-based CMOS devices. For very high-temperature applications, SiC complementary JFET (CJFET), which consists of a pair of normally-off p- and n-channel JFETs, has been proposed. Successful modeling of SiC CJFET by taking account of the incomplete ionization of dopants is also described.

articleTitle: Advances in GaN HEMT and GaN Power Amplifier Techniques for Base-Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE BiCMOS and Compound Semiconductor Integrated Circuits and Technology Symposium (BCICTS)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) technology has become the dominant solution for RF communication infrastructure applications for 5G networks and beyond. This paper presents application of our recently released $0.25 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ gate length GaN HEMT technology for enabling wideband operation of an integrated power amplifier module for 3.4-4.0 GHz operation delivering 32 dB gain and > 44% drain efficiency over the 600 MHz bandwidth in a small 10x6 mm$^{2}$ form factor, making it particularly suitable for 64T 5G mMIMO systems. In this contribution, we demonstrate how our technology performance improvements are leveraged for compelling product enhancements increasing the operating frequency range, gain and efficiency compared to our previous generation products.
